requirement_results.command: a fact ingested and watermarked at the same commit is served exactly, with served.canonical_commit and served.projection_watermark both equal to the required commit
a fact ingested into TypeDB but not yet watermarked fails closed with CONSISTENCY_DOWNGRADE under EXACT_AT_COMMIT, and the watermark itself is never falsely advanced

a fact whose row has been updated to a newer commit while the watermark still reads the older one fails closed with CONSISTENCY_DOWNGRADE when the older commit is requested exactly -- never silently serves the newer content mislabeled as the older, requested commit

AT_LEAST_COMMIT mode reports PROJECTION_NOT_READY (not a generic error) while behind, with the current watermark independently observable via a separate call, then succeeds once the watermark is advanced

across a real two-commit progression (ingest+watermark commit-1, read exact, ingest commit-2, read exact commit-1 again, watermark commit-2, read exact commit-2, read exact commit-1 again) the superseded commit is never served as exact once it is stale, in either direction

a query for a fact that was never ingested, at a watermark that honestly matches the required commit, reaches RESULT_NOT_FOUND rather than a falsified consistency failure -- consistency is checked before existence, not used to mask it
full local pytest regression, no new failures versus the pre-existing sandbox baseline (the two known interpreter-pin failures are unrelated and pre-existing)

residual_risks: This spike models projection lag with an explicit, test-driven advance_watermark step rather than a real asynchronous outbox consumer; it proves the READ-side contract enforcement is correct given any watermark/row state, not the specific timing of a production catch-up pipeline (which does not exist yet, per the same gap already disclosed in the Phase 3 language-migration decision for components 3-5).

TypeDB's `define` was empirically observed to be idempotent on this instance (redefining an identical schema is a no-op, not an error); this is a live-verified behavior of this TypeDB version, not a documented guarantee this spike asserts generally.

The @key constraint forces fact updates to be modeled as delete-then-insert (two transactions) rather than a single atomic update; a production projection writer would need its own concurrency discipline for that two-step sequence, which is out of this read-side spike's scope.
The same pre-existing local-venv gap noted in prior evidence (uv cannot resolve the exact 3.12.11 interpreter in this sandbox) is unchanged and out of this task's scope.

This task added a real, ephemeral TypeDB service container to 3 CI workflows (delivery-activation, rccad-methodology, validation-closure), mirroring the existing PostgreSQL service pattern exactly; every future PR now pulls one additional pinned image in those 3 jobs. This is the same category of change already made for PostgreSQL when OCOR-DEV-0015 was added, not a new precedent.
rollback_procedure_verified: Every test begins from adapter.reset() (a real delete of all spike-fact and spike-watermark instances against the live schema) and the schema itself is defined idempotently by initialize(), so a fresh run from a clean or partially-populated database converges to the same state -- verified directly by 5 consecutive full test-suite runs with no manual cleanup between them.
